title: Word order foundations
summary: Recognize the usual position of subject, verb, object, questions, and negatives.

title: Nouns, gender, and articles
summary: Learn how nouns interact with articles, number, gender, and definiteness.

title: Present time
summary: Describe identity, routine, repeated actions, and what is happening now.

title: Pronouns and reference
summary: Track who or what a sentence refers to without repeating every noun.

title: Negation essentials
summary: Make clear negative statements, commands, and short answers.

title: Numbers, time, and dates
summary: Use numbers with age, prices, clock time, dates, and quantities.

title: Questions that unlock conversation
summary: Build open and closed questions for people, places, time, reason, and method.

title: Past experiences
summary: Tell what happened, describe background, and connect events in a clear sequence.

title: Plans and predictions
summary: Express intention, arrangements, promises, probability, and future conditions.

title: Possession and belonging
summary: Show ownership, relationships, parts, and association naturally.

title: Requests, commands, and permission
summary: Ask for action, give directions, and request permission at the right level of politeness.

title: Place, movement, and prepositions
summary: Describe location, direction, origin, destination, and movement through space.

title: Comparison and degree
summary: Compare people and ideas, soften claims, and express meaningful differences.

title: Modality and politeness
summary: Use ability, permission, advice, obligation, probability, and polite distance.

title: Habit, duration, and frequency
summary: Explain how often, how long, and since when an action happens.

title: Relative information
summary: Add identifying or descriptive information about people, things, places, and times.

title: Reason, result, and purpose
summary: Connect events by explaining why something happened and what it was intended to achieve.

title: Complex sentences
summary: Connect cause, contrast, purpose, result, concession, and condition.

title: Reported language
summary: Report speech, thought, questions, and claims while preserving meaning and stance.

title: Conditional meaning
summary: Discuss real possibilities, imagined situations, regret, and mixed conditions.

title: Passive and impersonal structures
summary: Focus on an action, process, or result when the actor is unknown or less important.

title: Aspect and viewpoint
summary: Choose whether to present an action as complete, ongoing, repeated, or relevant now.

title: Style and emphasis
summary: Control information flow, focus, register, rhythm, and rhetorical impact.

title: Cohesion across paragraphs
summary: Guide readers and listeners through reference, substitution, connectors, and thematic progression.

title: Formal, neutral, and informal register
summary: Adapt grammar and vocabulary to professional, academic, friendly, and intimate contexts.

title: Information structure and focus
summary: Place known and new information strategically and highlight the element that matters.

title: Precision and nuance
summary: Choose forms for subtle certainty, implication, diplomacy, and voice.

title: Inference, stance, and evidentiality
summary: Signal evidence, confidence, distance, surprise, and responsibility for a claim.

title: Idiomatic grammar and fixed patterns
summary: Recognize structures whose natural meaning cannot be assembled word by word.

title: Editing for native-like control
summary: Revise ambiguity, repetition, rhythm, agreement, reference, and register with expert precision.

title: Agreement inside the phrase
summary: Keep articles, nouns, adjectives, pronouns, and verbs consistent where the language marks number, gender, or person.

title: Building useful noun phrases
summary: Combine quantity, description, ownership, and location into compact phrases you can reuse in real situations.

title: Connecting everyday ideas
summary: Link short messages with addition, contrast, choice, reason, result, and simple sequence.

title: Quantity and measurement
summary: Talk accurately about countable items, amounts, portions, distance, weight, and approximate quantity.

title: Narrative sequence and interruption
summary: Organize a story by separating background, main events, interruptions, and the final result.

title: Verbs with complements
summary: Choose the natural structure after common verbs: a noun, infinitive, clause, participle, or language-specific complement.

title: Focus through clause choice
summary: Choose active, passive, existential, and cleft-like structures according to what the listener already knows.

title: Managing distance and certainty
summary: Calibrate claims with probability, evidence, hedging, approximation, and polite distance.

title: Nominalisation and information density
summary: Package actions and qualities as noun phrases when formal or academic writing needs compact, connected information.

title: Parallelism and rhetorical balance
summary: Coordinate matching grammatical forms to make complex speech and writing clearer, more memorable, and more persuasive.

title: Strategic ambiguity and implication
summary: Recognize when grammar leaves agency, commitment, time, or evaluation implicit—and decide whether that effect is useful or misleading.

title: Grammar across dialect and genre
summary: Compare how conversation, journalism, academic prose, literature, and regional varieties reshape the same underlying message.

title: Core sentence order
summary: Build a dependable sentence frame and learn where the subject, action, object, time, and place normally appear.

title: Negatives and short answers
summary: Say no accurately, answer yes/no questions naturally, and avoid double-negation errors across languages.

title: Everyday prepositions and particles
summary: Choose natural markers for place, direction, time, transport, accompaniment, and purpose.

title: Requests, permission, and obligation
summary: Ask politely, give permission, express necessity, and distinguish strong rules from friendly advice.

title: Reported speech and viewpoint
summary: Report what someone said, asked, promised, or believed while keeping time and viewpoint clear.

title: Relative clauses for useful detail
summary: Identify people and things, add extra information, and avoid repeating short sentences.

title: Advanced conditionals and alternatives
summary: Discuss real possibilities, imagined situations, past regrets, mixed time, and alternatives to if.

title: Cohesion across a full paragraph
summary: Guide the reader through contrast, cause, reference, repetition, and topic development without sounding mechanical.

title: Stance in academic and professional writing
summary: Express confidence, caution, limitation, evaluation, and responsibility with precise grammatical choices.

title: Fronting, inversion, and marked emphasis
summary: Reshape normal word order to control emphasis, contrast, drama, and formal style without losing clarity.

title: Pragmatic grammar and implied meaning
summary: Interpret how grammar communicates politeness, irony, criticism, solidarity, hesitation, and meanings left unsaid.

title: Editing for native-like precision
summary: Diagnose subtle problems in agreement, information flow, idiomatic complementation, register, and rhythm.
